rationale: Constitutes the Central Information Commission; says nothing about an application made to the wrong public authority.
Section 6(3) requires an authority receiving an application for information held by another authority to transfer it within five days and inform the applicant.
Excludes intelligence organisations and sets a 45-day limit for human-rights information; a different time limit, not the 48-hour life-or-liberty rule.
Laying of rules before Parliament; unrelated to the 48-hour time limit.
Government education programmes and guide on RTI; does not address the 48-hour time limit.
A mentally ill person's right to information about their admission and treatment; a different Act and sense of information.
Severability of exempt parts of a record; does not deal with urgent time limits.
Exemptions from disclosure (including danger to life or safety as a ground to withhold); not the 48-hour time limit.
The proviso to section 7(1) requires information concerning life or liberty to be provided within forty-eight hours of the request.
Rule-making power on dangerous factory operations under the OSH Code; wrong Act and not the duty of persons handling hazardous substances under environmental law.
Government power to direct inquiries into workplace accidents; not about duties of persons handling hazardous substances.
National Board inquiry into extraordinary situations in hazardous-process factories; not a duty on handlers under environmental law.
Safety and security management for vessels and port facilities; unrelated to hazardous substance handling duties.
Workers' right to warn of imminent danger in hazardous-process factories under the OSH Code; similar topic but wrong Act and not the environmental-law duty.
Forbids any person to handle a hazardous substance except in accordance with prescribed procedure and safeguards.
Lets the Central Government delegate its powers under the Act; mentions its powers generally but not the power to issue directions.
Empowers the Central Government to issue binding directions, including closure, prohibition or regulation of any industry and stoppage of electricity or water.
Provides an appeal to the National Green Tribunal against directions issued under section 5.
Procedure of the Data Protection Board in inquiries; does not address when consent is required or what valid consent is.
Defines valid consent (free, specific, informed, unconditional, unambiguous), its presentation, withdrawal and consent managers.
Permits processing of personal data only for a lawful purpose with the Data Principal's consent or for legitimate uses, i.e. when consent is required.
Notice that must accompany or precede a request for consent; companion requirement for valid consent.
Powers and functions of the Data Protection Board; says nothing about children's personal data.
Requires verifiable parental consent before processing a child's data and bars tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising at children.
Restricts acceptance of foreign hospitality by legislators, judges and officials; same Act but not associations accepting foreign contributions.
Lets the Government prohibit dealing with currency accepted in contravention of the Act; enforcement on the topic but does not say whether or how associations may accept contributions.
A person granted a certificate or prior permission must receive foreign contribution only in the designated FCRA Account; companion procedure for accepting contributions.
Section 11 (registration or prior permission required for an association to accept foreign contribution) is the direct answer but is not admitted.
Section 12 (grant of certificate of registration or prior permission) is the companion procedure but is not admitted.
Applies the Act to vessels registered or required to be registered in India; mentions registration but does not say how a vessel is registered.
Sets who may own an Indian vessel and requires every Indian vessel to be registered at a notified port of registry.
Procedure for registration of Indian vessels, renewal, proof of title and grant of the certificate of registration by the Registrar.
Designates the Registrar of Indian vessels, the authority that registers vessels.
